purpose: Frozen i.i.d. hold-out slice of the real repo prose corpus (corpus B, C4/ATK-GATE-01).
selection_rule: sha256(relative_path) % 100 < 15, evaluated once against the corpus below and FROZEN.
discipline: FROZEN. Do not add/remove paths to move a number. Corpus A excludes exactly these; B is exactly these. Refresh only in its own PR with a rationale. Enforced: src.validation.corpus.load_holdout raises on a missing member rather than silently measuring a subset.
refresh_rationale: The 2026-07-19 slice lost members to remediation, not to selection. Two (docs/architecture/deprecated/README.md, .../batch.md) were deleted when the deprecated architecture tree was pruned; one (docs/archive/design-document.md) left the corpus when docs/archive/ was excluded as prose the project explicitly disowns. The old slice had silently shrunk 35 -> 33 with every hold-out test still green, which is the defect that prompted the fail-closed change. Re-applying the SAME unchanged hash rule to the current corpus keeps 32 of the previous 35 and admits 7 files that are new or moved. Membership is a function of the path, so it cannot be chosen; the previous manifest is retained beside this one as the record.
case_correction_2026_07_25: One frozen path read 'deprecated/batch.md'. The git index spells it 'BATCH.md'. The lowercase form resolved only on a case-insensitive filesystem, so corpus B silently loaded 34 of 35 members on Linux CI for as long as this manifest has existed — the membership was not actually frozen there. Found by the fail-closed check added the same day, on its first CI run. Path corrected to the index spelling; selection unchanged.
